findings.reason: Verified: pipeline.signature is md5 of the view class paths (pipeline/base.py:132-133), so it is the same for every session and the tests hardcode it; the OAuth state check gives no CSRF protection, unlike OAuth2AuthorizeView, which uses a random token bound to the session.

Verified: build_integration adds `sender` only when the state has one, and only the webhook passes it; the pipeline path calls ensure_integration, which overwrites metadata without `sender`, so a later reinstall into an orphaned Integration raises KeyError at `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` and returns a 500.

Verified: safe_urlopen sits outside the try and get_user_info calls raise_for_status with no wrapper, so a network failure or a GitHub error gives a 500 instead of the error page; real, but it only shows up when GitHub fails.

Verified: when Integration.DoesNotExist, the code goes to next_step() without any user check, so the new protection can be bypassed before the webhook is processed; this is a real gap in the new security control, but the window is narrow and the fix is a design choice.
Verified: the test uses state ddd023…, which does not match the constant signature 9cae5e…, so it fails at the state check and the 404 'installation could not be found' path is no longer covered.
